solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Do reduce your litter!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to do someone is to swindle them
second meaning, taken literally: a breeder who sells one puppy has one fewer in the litter

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads like a plea about rubbish; 'litter' is a dog's brood of puppies, and the phrase is also an idiom for a con.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell someone a pup is a British idiom for cheating them with a worthless purchase, which is what 'do' means as slang.

clue.text: Drive away reformed killer, perhaps, wiser after case dismissed

indicators.note: the shortened word comes after the other pieces

parts.note: someone reformed is an ex-criminal, giving EX
orc is a dictionary variant of orca, the killer whale

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, so dropping them leaves the inside

parts.note: taken as written, then its outer letters are removed

explanation.surface: A reformed murderer is driven out because he has become wiser after his case was dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case dismissed' sounds like a court ruling; it strips W and R from 'wiser'.
explanation.definitionFit: To exorcise is to expel an evil spirit, driving it out of a person or place.

clue.text: What shoppers do after failure to find cooking ingredient

indicators.note: the informing word comes after the failure word

parts.note: a lemon is a dud, something that fails
to shop someone is British slang for informing on them, and to grass is the same

explanation.surface: Shoppers turn to an alternative after not finding an ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoppers' are not customers: in British slang to shop someone is to betray them to the police, which is also to grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemongrass is a lemon-scented tropical grass used as a flavouring in South-East Asian dishes.

clue.text: Capital made of gossip — PC covered in shame

indicators.note: the computer and gossip are wrapped inside the regret word

parts.note: as in 'what a shame', pity
ana is a collection of anecdotes or table talk about someone
a Mac is a personal computer made by Apple

explanation.surface: A policeman embroiled in a gossipy scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a police constable; here it is a personal computer, a Mac.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama City is the capital of the Central American republic of Panama.

clue.text: Day trip in need of whacking great deposit

definitions.note: a rich deposit of ore worth mining

indicators.note: letters given a whacking are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A day out that needs a hefty payment up front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whacking great' reads as one phrase meaning huge; 'whacking' is the anagram signal and 'great deposit' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay dirt is ground rich enough in gold or ore to make mining profitable, so a valuable find.

clue.text: Jerk wanting nothing at first to do with loan request from Antony?

definitions.text: to do with loan request from Antony?
definitions.note: a description used as an adjective: relating to ears

indicators.note: the nothing comes at the front of the jerk

parts.note: O is nought, nothing
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A jerk who wants nothing to do with Antony asking for a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Antony's speech in Julius Caesar begins 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears', so his loan request is for ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is a medical adjective meaning relating to the ear, the thing Antony asked his audience to lend.

clue.text: Graduate getting zero on a stiff paper

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
nil means zero

explanation.surface: A graduate scores nothing on a tough exam paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff paper' looks like a hard exam; it is the definition, a strong brown paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Manila is strong brown paper, originally made from Manila hemp, used for envelopes and folders.

clue.text: Gifts the first thing Santa has for picking up?

indicators.note: picking up a sound is hearing it, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: Santa begins with a large, capital S, said aloud as large S

explanation.surface: Santa's first job is collecting presents to hand out.
explanation.walkthrough: The first thing in the name Santa is a capital letter, a large S; spoken, that gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generosity, or the money and presents freely given by a benefactor.

clue.text: Machine chopped fruit that a human regularly bags

definitions.note: the answer is the plural of automaton; the clue gives a singular, a looseness the blogger noted

indicators.note: to bag something is to capture it, so the outer letters hold the inner ones
taking letters at a regular interval means every other letter of human

parts.note: taken as written; its second and fourth letters are kept

indicators.note: a chopped word has lost its end, here the last letter of the fruit

parts.note: a tomato is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone carries off a chopped-up tomato in a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped' cuts the fruit's final letter, and 'regularly' keeps every other letter of 'human'; those two letters then bag the shortened fruit, with A in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Automata are self-operating machines or robots; the word is the plural of automaton.

clue.text: Standard, one consistently falling short

indicators.note: both pieces are cut short in the same way, each losing its final letter

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed right after 'Standard' in the clue is a comma
taken as written before it is shortened
the final letters of the two pieces, cut off as each falls short

explanation.surface: A standard that one keeps failing to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Standard' is itself part of the wordplay: COMMA and ONE both lose their last letters ('consistently falling short') to give COMM and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Common means ordinary or usual, which is what standard means as an adjective for everyday, regular things.

clue.text: Jack, with tyrant's role, taking time out — making it permanent?

definitions.note: the 'it' is the time out just described: a monarch who abdicates leaves the throne for good

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is AB, an able seaman

indicators.note: with 'out', says a letter is taken away from the role
with 'taking', the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a dictator's role is dictating

explanation.surface: A sailor plays a tyrant and takes a break, wondering whether to quit for good.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: 'taking time out' removes T, and doing that permanently, stepping down for good, is abdicating.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler who abdicates gives up the throne forever, a permanent version of stepping away from duty.

clue.text: Go free from Baltic?

indicators.note: the word free is taken away from the start of the cold word

parts.note: Baltic is Scottish slang for freezing cold
taken as written and removed

explanation.surface: Asks whether one can escape from the Baltic region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baltic' looks like the sea; in Scottish slang it means very cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Zing is energy or liveliness, the same sense as 'go' in 'full of go'.

clue.text: Tips on weapons hardware, so varied

indicators.note: varied means changed or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material
taken as written as anagram material

explanation.surface: Points about military hardware come in assorted kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowheads are the pointed tips fixed to the shafts of arrows, which are weapons.

clue.text: Vague desire maybe to get husband for Yankee lady at last

parts.note: a wish is an example of a desire
Yankee is Y in the radio alphabet
wanting H, husband, in place of the Yankee is wishing that 'Y was H', so these words supply WAS and H

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: taken as written; only its final letter is used

explanation.surface: An indecisive woman wants an American lover to become her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle is a phrase in disguise: a wish that Yankee (Y) were swapped for husband (H) reads as 'wish Y was H', and the last letter of 'lady' ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishy-washy means feeble, indecisive or lacking clear character, so vague.

clue.text: Animated cow in garden to barge in after hesitation

indicators.note: the barging-in word follows the hesitation

parts.note: erm is a sound of hesitation
to intrude is to barge in

explanation.surface: A cartoon cow pauses before barging into a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Ermintrude is the cow in The Magic Roundabout, a children's TV cartoon set in a magic garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermintrude is the flower-chewing cow of the British cartoon series The Magic Roundabout.

clue.text: 1000, say; slightly more ones and zeroes

definitions.note: a plural description of the binary digits that make up one megabit

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
say means for example, abbreviated EG
a bit more means slightly more

explanation.surface: A puzzle about counting a thousand and then a little more in binary.
explanation.definitionFit: A megabit is a million bits, binary digits each written as a one or a zero.

clue.text: Force king to accept a top politician's charter

indicators.note: the force word takes in the other letters

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them
the Prime Minister is the top politician, abbreviated PM
R is rex, king

explanation.surface: A monarch is forced to accept a political leader's charter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charter' looks like a constitutional document; it is one who charts.
explanation.definitionFit: A charter in this sense is someone who draws charts, and a map-maker draws maps or charts.

clue.text: A quiet moment with the French chap behind the museum?

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
a mo is a moment
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A quiet moment with a Frenchman at the back of a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: Elias Ashmole's collection founded the Ashmolean Museum in Oxford, so he is the man behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elias Ashmole was the seventeenth-century collector whose gift founded Oxford's Ashmolean Museum.

clue.text: Low calorie helping reduced by a third, people learned

parts.note: lite describes a low-calorie product

indicators.note: two of the six letters are cut off, leaving two thirds

parts.note: a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: Educated people take a low-calorie portion cut by a third.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are well-read, educated people, especially those with literary interests.

clue.text: Old sailor wearing light, tight garment

indicators.note: the light has the sailor on it as a garment, so it surrounds those letters

parts.note: an LED is a light
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: An old seaman in a light, figure-hugging outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has the sailor wearing a light outfit, but in the wordplay it is the light that wears the old sailor, wrapped round him.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is a close-fitting one-piece garment worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: Elders quietly replaced by trees next to railway

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: replaced here means put back in a different place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material
taken as written as anagram material

explanation.surface: Old men are quietly swapped for trees beside a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elders' could be elder trees beside the trees in the surface; here they are church elders.
explanation.definitionFit: In Presbyterian churches the presbytery is the governing body made up of elders.

clue.text: Come to a halt by front of pub in Ireland

indicators.note: the letters go inside the name of the country

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
X is the multiplication sign, as in three by four

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of pub is used

explanation.surface: Coming to a stop beside an Irish pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' gives X as in measurements, three by four.
explanation.definitionFit: To expire is to end or run out, as a contract or licence does when it comes to a halt.

clue.text: Where cricketers practise catches

definitions.meaning: first meaning: practice pitches enclosed by netting
second meaning: a verb, traps as in a net

explanation.walkthrough: 'Catches' looks like what the cricketers practise, but it is a separate verb meaning traps.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket nets are netted practice lanes, and to net something is to catch or trap it.

clue.text: Bloomer, with Latin stars receiving letter from Greek detectives

indicators.note: the Latin word takes in the other letters, as a host receives a guest

parts.note: astra is Latin for stars
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
DIs are detective inspectors

explanation.surface: A blunder involving Latin stars and Greek detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake; it is a plant that flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy flowering houseplant, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Hint — minor — that's dropped every so often

indicators.note: letters are dropped at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: taken as written; every other letter, starting with the second, is kept

explanation.surface: A slight clue, which gets omitted now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota is a tiny amount, as in 'not an iota of truth', so a mere trace or hint.

clue.text: Evidently need oil pipe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hinge that ... shows it needs oiling
second meaning: to pipe is to make a thin high-pitched sound

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' looks like plumbing that needs oil; it is a verb for a shrill sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeak is the high, thin noise of an unlubricated hinge, and also a short shrill cry like a piped note.

clue.text: Link with Brussels bureaucrat so ruefully if partially recalled

definitions.note: the train service connecting London with Brussels

indicators.note: called back, so the letters are taken in the opposite direction
only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: An EU official ruefully recalls a link with Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters RATSORUE sit inside 'bureaucrat so ruefully'; turned round they spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurostar is the high-speed rail service through the Channel Tunnel connecting London to Brussels and Paris.

clue.text: Poet's light, mostly obscene book

definitions.note: read as 'the poet is', the 's linking definition and wordplay

parts.note: day means daylight

indicators.note: most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: lewd means obscene
Is is the abbreviation for the Book of Isaiah

explanation.surface: A poet's light verse turns out to be a mostly obscene book.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Day-Lewis was an Anglo-Irish writer who became Britain's Poet Laureate in 1968.
